title: Stream-aware active-active failover playbook for hosted edge gateways
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Goal: Define and implement a tested active-active failover playbook for the hosted API edge/gateway that preserves streaming session continuity, respects SLOs, and provides deterministic load-shedding and circuit-breaker behavior during region degradation or capacity loss.

Context: Redwood's hosted API runs globally with region-local edge gateways. We need an operationally simple, automatable failover strategy that does not break long-running streaming sessions (WebSocket / SSE / HTTP rpcs with chunked streaming), minimizes p99 latency regression, and avoids cascading overload on healthy regions. Existing tickets focus on traffic steering and soft cutovers but do not cover a combined SLO-driven decision flow that ties routing, KV cache sync, and layered load-shedding into a single playbook.

Key constraints and assumptions:
- Sessions may carry large KV cache state (model key-value caches used for session affinity).
- Streaming sessions are long-lived (tens of seconds to minutes); some customers expect uninterrupted streams for real-time use cases.
- Routing decisions must be quick (<100ms decision window) and observable.
- Destination regions can advertise operational capacity and degrade progressively (normal -> degraded -> emergency).
- Cannot rely on cross-region synchronous KV writes at scale; we will use snapshot + progressive replay for session rehydration when possible.

Primary deliverables:
1) Failover decision engine spec (SLO-driven state machine) that emits routing actions: drain, redirect, mirror, or reject-with-backoff.
2) Circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis tuned for streaming: separate short-window error rate for handshake failures and long-window disconnect rate.
3) Session rehydration strategy: prefix-cache snapshot + delta fetch with optimistic replay on target region.
4) Layered load-shedding policy: gateway-level (coarse), model-variant fallback (graceful degradation), application-level soft-denial (error+hint), and token-based throttling.
5) Runbook for on-call with automated rollback and manual override knobs in Console.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- During an injected degradation in region-us-east, at least 95% of streaming sessions either resume on a secondary region without user-visible gaps >500ms, or receive a client-visible graceful degradation notice with suggested retry behavior.
- End-to-end SLOs: availability >= 99.9% global for non-stream endpoints; stream continuity >= 99.0% per-session success in failover tests.
- No more than 2x increase in p99 latency in the backing region under controlled failover tests.
- Circuit-breaker engages before headroom-consuming cascade; false-positive tripping <1% during normal load.

Design decisions made so far:
- Traffic shift model: weight-based gradual shift (exponential moving over N seconds with per-session affinity check). Mirror mode may be used for warm-up but not for write-paths.
- Session affinity: session binding key (session_id + client_token hash) used to locate KV snapshots. Primary region periodically publishes compact snapshot metadata to a regional metadata store (eventual-consistent).
- Rehydration: target region attempts to fetch most recent snapshot via cross-region pull; if snapshot age > threshold OR fetch fails, fallback to model-variant degraded path (stateless continuation or truncated context) with an explicit client header indicating degraded-mode.
- Circuit breaker: three-tier circuit: (1) short-window handshake errors (>5% in 30s), (2) medium-window disconnects (>3% in 5m), (3) capacity pressure via queue length and GPU utilization (>85%). Trip levels are combined with exponential backoff and a staggered re-probe schedule per-region.
- Load shedding: prefer graceful shedding (403 with Retry-After and recovery hints) for best-effort clients, and hard shedding for internal high-priority customers only when capacity exhausted. Token-based priorities propagate through the edge to ensure reserved customers can >= keep minimal throughput.

Open technical trade-offs / risks:
- Cross-region snapshot pulls add latency and transient load to healthy regions. We mitigate with caching and rate-limiting but must measure.
- Guaranteeing <500ms resume may be impossible for some sessions with massive KV state. We will define per-customer/reservation SLOs and advertise limitations.
- Complexity of state machine increases operational burden. We'll cap state transitions and prefer coarse-grained statuses: OK / DEGRADED / EMERGENCY.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize state machine + circuit-breaker thresholds; prototype decision engine in edge-router service. (Owner: Jonah)
- Week 2: Implement session snapshot metadata publisher and cross-region snapshot pull with cache layer. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- Week 3: Instrument new metrics and dashboards (stream-resume-rate, session-handoff-latency, region-degrade-index). (Owner: Carlos Mendes)
- Week 4: End-to-end canary test: inject region degradation in staging, execute gradual weight shifts, measure acceptance criteria. Fix any regressions. (Owner: Reliability team)

Notes on observability and dashboards:
- New dashboard widgets: per-region stream-handshake-failure-rate, per-session resume-time histogram, model-variant-fallback-rate, circuit-breaker-state-timeline.
- Alerts: Pager if stream-resume-rate drops below 98% for more than 5 minutes; SEV if circuit-breaker is open in >1 region concurrently for >2m and customer-impacted traffic >1%.

- [x] Decision engine spec document (v0.1)
- [x] Threshold proposal review with SRE & Runtime
- [ ] Edge-router prototype merged (PR 2145)
- [ ] Snapshot metadata publisher in runtime merged

Rollout plan:
- Begin with internal-only canary traffic (10% of internal org) -> expand to beta customers -> regional public canary (1%) -> ramp to 10% -> full adopting region handling. Automate rollback when key metrics cross thresholds for longer than 2 minutes.

Postmortem / follow-up items (anticipated):
- Investigate session snapshot size bloat and potential streamlining (token compression).
- Evaluate use of opportunistic state forwarding (pre-warming target region caches before redirect) to reduce resume time.
- Tighten client-facing SDK behavior for automated reconnection with exponential backoff and jitter.
